$comment: AMH machine mode for Claude Code: a USER-LEVEL settings fragment. It is never a project file and amh-init.sh never installs it. To install it, copy scripts/command-guard.sh byte for byte to ~/.claude/hooks/amh-command-guard.sh, then merge the deny entries and the PreToolUse group below into ~/.claude/settings.json by hand, keeping whatever that file already holds; do not replace it. Managed settings are the stronger place for the same fragment where you administer them: a project cannot override them, and --restricted still loads them. The hook runs the guard's --machine mode on every Bash and PowerShell call in every session on this machine. That mode keeps only the permanent deletion denials (the filesystem root, a home directory, a Windows drive root, and a cmd /c recursive deletion carrying nested escaped quotes), the credential rails, and the guard's refusals to pass a command it could not read. It drops AMH's push, forge, hook-file and one-time rails and reads no amh.conf, because those are a project's process; inside an AMH repository the project guard still applies them. onFailure block makes a guard that cannot run refuse the call, as the project adapter does, so remove this hook entry BEFORE deleting the script or every shell call in every session is refused; on Windows that also means Git for Windows is required, and $HOME is the Git Bash home, normally your user profile. The deny rails are the project adapter's credential Read rails (with the /proc rails also spelled from the filesystem root, //proc, since a single leading slash in a settings file names a path beside that file), its two commands that print a stored credential, and an Edit rail on the installed guard, which reaches the file-editing tools but not a cp or mv. What this is not: containment (a container, a VM or an account that cannot write the disk is), or a rail any repository can see, so no ladder checks the installed copy's version and you refresh it by hand after an upgrade. Claude Code's --safe-mode and --bare skip a user-level hook like any settings hook, and --restricted ignores the user settings file, though not managed settings (AMH ledger row DD063).

hooks.command: bash "$HOME/.claude/hooks/amh-command-guard.sh" --machine # AMH machine mode. On Windows it requires Git Bash: install Git for Windows
